title: Hybrid kernel handoff causes intermittent token duplication and FP32 accumulation skew during burst prefill
creator: Aisha Patel
description: During high-throughput prefill bursts we observed rare but reproducible correctness issues: duplicated output tokens for a subset of requests and small but accumulating numerical drift in logits when the runtime transitions between the fused-attention kernel and the fallback kernel (hybrid handoff). These manifest only under bursty prefill patterns when the handoff occurs mid-stream and the accumulator path changes precision or ordering. The issue appears tied to the kernel handoff handshake not establishing a deterministic accumulator/sequence context, causing replayed decode slices and non-deterministic FP32 accumulation ordering across kernels.
reproduction_steps: 1) Use model: redwood/open-fused-test@v2 (test harness included in PR-XYZ)
2) Generate prefill-heavy traffic: 256 concurrent prefill streams with synthetic prompt length 512 and burst schedule 50ms on/100ms off
3) Enable hybrid kernel routing (fused preferred, fallback allowed) and mixed-precision accumulators
4) Observe outputs across >10k requests: look for duplicated tokens sequences and tiny divergent logit sums compared to golden-run on stable kernel
5) Reproduce locally with debug build and KERNEL_HANDOFF_TRACE=1 to capture handshake traces
investigation_notes: - Initial triage (2026-02-19): duplicates correlated with handoffs recorded in scheduler trace; no issues when forcing single kernel path.
- Memory snapshots show identical KV cache pointers but differing accumulator state when handoff completes during an in-flight decode slice.
- FP drift: observed consistent small positive bias in logits after handoff when accumulator used FP32 vs FP16 accumulation path ordering.
- Race window identified between scheduler's 'complete_prefill' event and kernel swap commit; race allows decode slice to be re-enqueued on fallback path without clearing transient decode flags.
- Deterministic repro added to fuzz harness (tests/runtime/handoff_fuzz.cc), reproduces duplication within 2k runs on CI-size workload after seeding scheduler jitter.
- Profiling indicates handshake currently performs non-atomic update of sequence_id and accumulator_version (two separate writes).
root_cause: Atomicity gap in the kernel handoff handshake: sequence/stream identity and accumulator metadata are updated non-atomically. Under burst prefill scheduling, a decode slice can be acknowledged by the scheduler and then re-routed to a fallback kernel that expects a different accumulator ordering, causing the fallback to replay or duplicate tokens and leading to small FP numeric drift because accumulation order/precision differs between kernels.
workaround: Disable hybrid handoff by forcing a single kernel path (set KERNEL_ROUTING=force_fused or force_fallback) or serialize handoffs by increasing the HandoffGraceWindow to avoid mid-slice transitions. Not ideal for throughput but mitigates correctness regressions.
mitigation_plan: 1) Make handshake atomic: introduce a single 64-bit handshake token (sequence_id + accumulator_version) updated atomically and verified by receiving kernel (owner-based commit)
2) Add deterministic accumulator policy: canonicalize accumulation to FP32 with Kahan-style correction on handoff boundary to remove ordering bias
3) Ensure decode slice is quiesced before handoff commit: prevent re-enqueue of the same slice during handshake window
4) Add regression tests: fuzz harness, long-run canary with burst traffic (1M tokens), and unit tests that simulate interleaved handoffs
5) Roll out change behind runtime flag KERNEL_HANDOFF_ATOMIC=true and perform staged canary on dedicated pools
6) Post-deploy: run nightly stability job comparing golden outputs and drift metrics; gate change by zero-duplication and drift < 1e-6 average per-token logit delta
